venue.name: Sointula Museum
venue.description: The Sointula Museum tells the story of Malcolm Island and of the Finnish settlement of Sointula, from its utopian beginnings to commercial fishing, unions and cooperative economic structures. It sits in the old Superior School Building at 280 1st Street, which it shares with the local library, and fills three exhibition rooms with artifacts, photographs, books, maps and archives. The displays are hands-on, so visitors can pump the 1905 foghorn from Pulteney Point Lighthouse, browse the Co-op store counters and use the first bilingual switchboard in British Columbia. Admission is by donation with a suggested minimum of $5.00 per person, and guided tours for groups and school classes are offered year round by arrangement.

facility_notes.washrooms: The washroom and galleries on the main floor are accessible.
facility_notes.lunch_space: There is no food or drink allowed in the museum.
facility_notes.stroller_accessible: Strollers are permitted in the museum, but please note that some aisles are narrow. We will be happy to store your stroller during your visit. Please let the Visitor Services staff member know that you would like to park a stroller.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: The museum is wheelchair and walker accessible using a ramp leading into the building. The washroom and galleries on the main floor are accessible. The 'Rust Room' on the lower level of the museum can be reached through a downstairs door. Please make arrangements with visitor services to open the downstairs door.
facility_notes.bus_parking: Parking is free in both the parking lots in front of and behind the museum.

restrictions: There is no food or drink allowed in the museum.
Still photography is permitted for private, non-commercial use only. Photographs cannot be published, sold, reproduced, transferred, distributed or otherwise commercially exploited in any manner.
Wheelchairs are permitted in the museum. We do not have a wheelchair on site to lend visitors.
All tours must be pre-booked in advance.

Sointula is on Malcolm Island and is reached by boat. To reach the museum, either on foot or by car, turn left off the ferry and proceed three blocks (350 meters) to a bend in the road. The Superior School is located on the left (waterside).
venue.hours_notes: Summer hours, June 1 to September 15: open daily 12pm to 4pm. Winter hours, September 16 to May 31: Tuesdays, Thursdays and Saturdays 12pm to 3pm. Admission is by donation. Outside those hours the museum opens by appointment.
venue.seasonal_notes: Guided tours are offered year round and must be pre-booked. For groups of 5 or more people who want to visit the museum outside of regular summer open hours, the museum asks you to call or text 250-230-9650 to arrange a special time and tour guide.

programs.name: School group guided tour
programs.description: A guided tour of the exhibitions for a class, led by the museum's volunteers. The exhibitions can cover technology, early Finnish settler history, fishing, the development of a small community and more, and the museum will shape the tour around what the class needs. Tour length varies and the museum recommends about an hour. Tours run year round and all of them must be pre-booked. The price is $5.00 per child with two accompanying adults free.
programs.what_children_do: Walk three exhibition rooms with a guide, looking at Finnish settlers' belongings, the Co-op store counters, photo albums and the fishing, logging and farming gear in the Rust Room. They can try the real 1905 foghorn from Pulteney Point Lighthouse, use the first bilingual switchboard in British Columbia, and sit in the media centre to watch short videos about island life.
programs.our_note: The whole visit is indoors and the museum suggests about an hour, so it suits a class that can look and listen rather than run. The foghorn sits in the Rust Room on the lower level, which is opened by staff through a separate downstairs door, so ask for it to be open before you arrive. Getting there means a ferry to Malcolm Island and then a 350 metre walk left from the dock, so build the crossing into your day.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms are on site, the main floor is step free by a ramp, and strollers are allowed although some aisles are narrow. No food or drink is allowed inside, so lunch has to happen somewhere else, and nothing is published about parking a bus or about how many children can come at once.
programs.extra_fees_note: Two accompanying adults come free. Their tours page prices each additional adult at $8.00.
programs.evidence: School groups are $5.00/child with 2 accompanying adults free.

programs.name: Guided group tour
programs.description: A guided tour of the exhibitions led by the museum's volunteers, digging into the early Finnish settlers' experiences. The museum describes it as about 45 minutes and ideal for groups of 5 or more, and says guests are welcome to stay and enjoy the museum before or after the tour. Tours run year round and must be pre-booked. The price on their visit page is $6.00 per person. Groups of 5 or more can also call or text to arrange a time outside the regular summer opening hours.
programs.what_children_do: Follow a volunteer through three exhibition rooms of settlers' belongings, Co-op store counters, photo albums and fishing, logging and farming gear, then stay on afterwards to watch videos in the media centre or pump the 1905 foghorn in the Rust Room.
programs.our_note: Forty five minutes is the published length and the rooms are small, so a big group will move through in waves. Outside the summer the museum is open three afternoons a week, so a tour on any other day has to be arranged by phone or text first.
programs.practical_summary: Everything happens indoors on one main floor, with washrooms on site and a ramp at the door. Food and drink are not allowed inside, and the museum does not publish a maximum group size or any notice period, so settle both when you call.
programs.evidence: these 45-minute-ish guided tours delve into the early Finnish settlers’ experiences

programs.name: Self-guided visit and Museum Detective Challenge
programs.description: The museum is open to drop-in visitors during its posted hours and admission is by donation, with a suggested minimum of $5.00 per person. Three exhibition rooms hold hands-on displays and the media centre has a seating area with twelve self-guided videos. The Museum Detective Challenge is free and comes in two versions depending on reading level, and is picked up at the visitor services desk. There is also a hands-on lesson on operating a real lighthouse foghorn.
programs.what_children_do: Pick up a free detective challenge at the visitor services desk and work the clues through the exhibition rooms, then colour in a Sointula Museum Detective Certificate with the museum's crayons and pencil crayons. They can pump the 1905 Pulteney Point foghorn, browse the Co-op store counters, use the first bilingual switchboard in British Columbia and sit in the media centre to watch short videos.
programs.our_note: This is the cheapest way to bring a small group, but admission is by donation rather than free, so agree what you will give before you arrive. The challenge comes in two reading levels, which helps when the children are a range of ages. Nothing can be eaten or drunk inside, so plan lunch elsewhere.
programs.practical_summary: A short indoor visit at your own pace, with washrooms and a step free main floor, and a seated media room if the children need a rest. The site sets no price, no age and no group size for a drop-in visit, so ask what a donation should look like for a group.
programs.extra_fees_note: Admission to the museum is by donation (suggested minimum is $5.00/person). The detective challenge itself is free.
programs.evidence: Pick up your free detective challenge at the visitor services desk.

no youngest age is stated, and nothing on the site addresses preschool or daycare groups

no maximum group size is published for any tour, and no minimum group size is set for a school class; the 5 or more figure is described as ideal for the general group tour and as the threshold for arranging a visit outside summer opening hours
no minimum notice is published; the tours page says only that all tours must be pre-booked in advance

school group pricing differs between their visit page and their tours page, $5.00 per child against $6.00 per youth. The visit page was last updated 2024-03-21 and the tours page 2024-03-20 according to the site's own page listing, so the visit page figure is the one recorded

the general group tour price also differs between the two pages, $6.00 per person against $6.00 per youth and $8.00 per adult. The youth figure agrees on both pages and is recorded; the adult figure is not
no year or season is attached to any price; both pages carrying prices were last updated in March 2024, so the figures may be older than they look
the opening season differs between the body of the visit page and the panel that runs at the bottom of every page
there is no indoor lunch space. Food and drink are not allowed in the museum, and no picnic area, park or alternative eating place is mentioned anywhere on the site
nothing is published about bus parking; the site mentions only free parking in the lots in front of and behind the museum
nothing is published about quiet or sensory friendly times, or about support for neurodiverse visitors
no coordinates are published anywhere on the site and there is no map embed, so the pin comes from geocoding the published street address

the photographs on the site carry no alt text and several are page background images rather than inline pictures. No browser was used in this run, so each alt was written from the file name and the caption printed on the page rather than from looking at the image

the ferry crossing to Malcolm Island is part of any visit. The site links BC Ferries schedules but publishes no crossing time, fare or sailing frequency, and that decides whether a group can come at all
admission is by donation with a suggested minimum of $5.00 per person; the site does not say whether children are expected to give it
the Rust Room, which holds the 1905 foghorn, is on the lower level behind a downstairs door that has to be opened by staff, and the site does not say whether there is a lift or only stairs
no deposit, payment timing or cancellation terms are published for a group tour
